html:
Abitibiwinni Aki is the homeland of the Abitibiwinni, an Anishinaabe people of the Lake Abitibi region in western Quebec and northeastern Ontario. They are one of the Algonquin nations. The name Abitibi is usually explained as "halfway water", as the lake lies near the height of land between rivers running north to James Bay and south toward the St. Lawrence.

They hunted, trapped and fished across the boreal forest. From the 1600s the lake lay on canoe routes between New France and the Hudson's Bay Company posts on James Bay, and both sides wanted their furs. To the north lived the Cree. Today the Abitibiwinni First Nation lives mainly at Pikogan, near Amos, Quebec.
